## Summary
Committing to this repo requires conforming messages and structure-clean code: type(scope): subject ≤72 chars; fix commits need Regression/Class/Sweep trailers (class from .mivia/quality/defect-taxonomy.md, e.g. DC-13); pre-commit runs check_go_structure.py --strict --staged where soft limits (500 file/80 func/800 test-file) become hard — no --no-verify, no baseline raises.

## What did not work
- Attempting to commit with the git UI-style long subject fails the commit-msg hook (subject >72 chars or non-conforming type).\n- git commit without staging first fails silently (exit 1, nothing committed) — always git add -A first.\n- git add -A sweeps the concurrent agent's untracked files into your commit — stage only your paths when sharing a tree.

## Why
The workspace enforces these gates via scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit and pre-push; knowing them upfront avoids failed-commit round trips and accidental capture of a peer agent's work. # Orchestration guardrails: sub-agents stall without committing

scope: project
verdict: mixed
tags: orchestration, spawn_agent, guardrails, commit-discipline, concurrent-writer
created: 2026-08-13

## Summary
Spawned go-engineer agents stalled twice on multi-feature tasks: s3 looped 30+ min on test fixes without committing; s5 ended its run having staged (git add) but never committed. Both required root takeover to finalize. Hard guardrails fixed it: commit-first-green, hard time-boxes (20-25 min), max 2 fix attempts then stop-and-report.

## What worked
- Commit-first-green guardrail produced fast, clean commits (s6b done in 2 min)
- Steer with interrupt=true successfully broke s3 out of its loop
- Checking git status + staged diff at run end recovered s5's staged work
- Full-tree fresh verification (go test -count=1 ./...) caught everything before reporting done

## What did not work
- s3 ran 30+ min with no commit, no parks, no retries — silent spin
- s5 staged its commit but the task completed without finalizing it
- Docs agent never committed its deliverables (had to be committed by root)
- Event ledger records only start events; completion is invisible there — git log is ground truth

## Why
Large spawned tasks (controller admission, driver CLI) loop silently on failing tests — no parks/retries/blocked events appear, so the event ledger gives no signal. Work is at risk from a concurrent writer that restores older file snapshots; uncommitted files can vanish. Root must verify git status + index state at run end, not just task statuses: staged-but-uncommitted work is common (s5 staged 1356 lines then ended). Always include explicit commit instructions in every task prompt (docs agents won't commit otherwise) and re-verify the final tree yourself.

# Panel review context: recency ordering + cap tightening (research-backed)

scope: project
verdict: good
tags: panel, context, review, lost-in-the-middle, workflows
created: 2026-08-13

## Summary
Context management for panel reviews: reordered the 6 panel member templates so instructions lead and the review target (findings + implementation) sits at the end (recency beats lost-in-the-middle), and tightened bug-fix.toml binding caps (scope 4K, findings 16K). Members already use the industry-standard patterns (structured outputs, parallel specialization, selective fetch).

## What worked
- Template text controls binding render order (template.Render expands {{ }} in file order): "lost in the middle" (arXiv 2307.03172) is fixable by reordering sections — instructions first, review target (findings/implementation) last, plan in the middle
- Envelope-only bindings (prior_findings 4096B) are the established sharing mechanism; step-level bindings feed ALL panel members + the post-panel review step (do not remove them as "dead" — synthesis just doesn't render them)
- Members already follow the industry pattern: structured JSON output schemas, parallel domain specialization, selective file fetch via read tools (diff-only + fetch)
- Tightened bug-fix.toml caps: scope 16000→4096, findings 32768→16384 (worst-case reduction; typical content unaffected)
- Contract tests assert member config paths only, not template content — template reordering is test-safe

## What did not work
- Compaction/summarization is lossy and compounds (Claude Code ~20K token summary reservation; Codex compaction fragile) — use as last resort, not primary strategy
- Per-member binding scoping (security gets no plan) is an engine change (step-level bindings are shared) — deferred
- "Avrix" is NOT a code review product; only an AI-infrastructure firm (avrix.com) — user likely meant Aider/CodeRabbit-class tools

## Why
Industry research (Claude Code/Aider/Cline/Codex/Cursor + G-Research, arXiv 2307.03172) shows focused prompts beat long ones and the most important content must be at the start/end. Our pipeline already had structured context, envelopes, and per-member specialization; the two real wins were ordering and worst-case caps. Compaction was rejected as lossy; per-member binding scoping deferred (engine change).

created: 2026-08-13

## Summary
CORRECTION: on_diff_size_failure is a [delivery] repair-STEP name, never a dead-fail enum. An over-limit diff is a repairable DiffSizeError routed to the repair step (fallback on_failure): the agent shrinks/splits the chunk, delivery retries, bounded by max_repairs. The run is never failed for size alone.

## What worked
- Verified ground truth in code before answering: types.go Delivery.OnDiffSizeFailure (step name), delivery/repair.go RepairTarget (DiffSizeError -> OnDiffSizeFailure -> OnFailure), delivery/stacking.go checkChunkDiffSize (repairable DiffSizeError), controller linear_diff_gate.go (post-implement reroute to the repair step).
- Corrected docs/architecture/workflows.md + docs/product/workflows-guide.md (removed the bogus [stacking] key; added the [delivery] table row).
- Strengthened repair.md + bugfix-repair.md: a DIFF-SIZE rejection is a SPLIT request - shrink the delivered diff, record deferred scope in summary for a follow-up chunk, never silently drop scope.

## What did not work
- My earlier summary/memory claimed an enum on_diff_size_failure = shrink_retry|reroute_fail_fast with a dead-fail mode. That enum DOES NOT EXIST in the code: on_diff_size_failure is a [delivery] knob naming a repair STEP (same pattern as on_failure/on_pr_metadata_failure). The docs I wrote for it were wrong and have been corrected.
- A single inline run can only SHRINK its own delivered diff; turning deferred scope into additional PRs is the stacking driver's (mivia stack plan/drive) job - be explicit about that boundary rather than implying a single run re-chunks.

## Why
The user caught a real misinformation bug: my docs/summary claimed the system can dead-fail a run for an oversized PR, which is the opposite of what the code does and of what they asked for. Recording the verified semantics prevents repeating the error and documents the honest boundary (single-run shrink vs driver-driven multi-PR breakdown).

## Summary
mivia release is tag-triggered (release.yml, push tags v*): validate -> build 6-matrix -> gh release create. No release branch; tag created manually on master after merge. Installers resolve latest via releases/latest/download/mivia-version.txt (stable only). Pre-merge review 2026-08-10: no reachable bugs; 5 action pins advisory-clean; attest-build-provenance v2.4.0 is last v2.

## What worked
- Verified executable checks: YAML parse OK, bash -n OK, py_compile OK, make release-test PASS, go run ./cmd/mivia version --json returns {"binary":"mivia","version":"0.0.0-dev"} matching the workflow assertions
- installers are fail-closed: strict semver, checksum format (64 hex + exact name + uniqueness), archive entry allowlist, staged atomic install
- Security review found no reachable command injection: tag flows via env vars; semver regex rejects shell metachars; all five pinned action SHAs are current-major, advisory-clean

## What did not work
- Reviewer agent hallucinated a blocker (claimed install.sh used bash [[ under #!/bin/sh; verified false - it is POSIX-only). Always verify agent claims against the actual file
- Security MAJORs: validate job's rev-parse equality is trivially true for tag pushes (github.sha == tag commit), proving nothing about review/CI; pipeline creates SLSA attestations but never verifies them; installers verify SHA-256 against same-host unsigned manifest (integrity, not authenticity)
- attest-build-provenance pin is a tag-object SHA, not a commit SHA; v2 line is EOL

## Why
Records the verified state of the release pipeline so future release work starts from facts: tag-driven flow, review verdict, advisory status of pins (correcting the non-existent CVE-2025-26367/30226 premises). Also documents that a reviewer's 'install.sh uses [[ under #!/bin/sh' blocker was a false positive - install.sh is pure POSIX sh.

# Harness hardening: loop caps, delete_file tool, delivery retry+error surfacing, .mivia/runs traces

scope: project
verdict: good
tags: workflows, harness, durability, delivery, repair-loops, delete-file
created: 2026-08-11

## Summary
Root-caused and fixed three harness defects found by 11 parallel workflows: (1) unbounded review loops with no agent file-deletion primitive and disabled stall guard, (2) delivery stuck at delivery_pending after OOM-killed push with invisible error hints and no retry, (3) .mivia/runs never created/populated for workflow runs.

## What worked
- Bounded all 9 repair loops in feature-delivery.toml (5/8 caps) so the stall guard activates (identical findings 3x -> durable 'no progress' failure)
- Added delete_file tool (refuses dirs/symlinks/escapes/root; declared 4096 budget; worst-case harness exercised) + registered for workflow-engineer
- Delivery push now retries 3x with backoff; delivery error text is resolved into workflow_status (ErrorText) and the CLI/on-disk summaries
- Engine now creates .mivia/runs and writes a bounded per-run JSON summary at admission/resume/terminal/delivery (namespace single-sourced via workspace.NamespacePath)
- Merged the two stuck runs' completed work into local master (e362867 config load fix, 6c26719 context planner fix) and deleted their ledger records

## What did not work
- Run 6 looped 50 review rounds: workflow-engineer agent lacks any file-deletion primitive, reviewer demanded deleting a leftover bom_test.go (host action), review_repair was unbounded (max_iterations=-1) which disables the identical-findings stall guard in linear_convergence.go, and cancel is refused while a live executor claim (5-min lease) is held
- Runs 7/10 stuck at delivery_pending: the delivery push runs the repo's full pre-push verify (make verify) and the process was SIGKILLed mid-hook under 11 parallel runs (OOM); no automatic retry; the stored error ref (sha256:...) was not readable via ledger_read, so the failure hint was invisible
- workflow_cancel returns 'claimed by another executor' while the engine holds a fresh claim; a retry at a step boundary (claim released between attempts) succeeded

## Why
The 11 parallel feature-delivery runs exposed harness gaps that cost hours and needed manual intervention. Each fix closes a distinct mechanism: unbounded loops disable the controller's own stall guard; agents without a deletion primitive cannot satisfy file-removal findings; delivery failures record hints in a form no tool resolves and never retry; and the documented trace directory is never created. These are durable product fixes, not one-off workarounds.

# TUI composer Up-history overlay: validated plan and codebase facts

scope: project
verdict: good
tags: tui, bubbletea, history, overlay, keymap, adlc, internal/cli
created: 2026-08-11

## Summary
Validated plan for a TUI composer history overlay (Up at cursor origin opens 3-row picker of sent messages). Key facts: bubbles textarea has no history; Session.Messages is pruned + commits at turn end; skill display strings are stored in session; reuse the suggest-popup overlay pattern; sanitize overlay rows with SafeChatBlockText (ANSI/OSC injection); reset sentHistory on every session change.

## What worked
- Up at (0,0) in the composer is currently a complete no-op (bubbles textarea CursorUp clamps); interception point is handleChatKey right after handleSuggestKey, handler contract (bool,bool,[]tea.Cmd), consume -> (true,true,nil).
- Reuse suggest overlay pattern: renderDialogFrame + overlayAt + suggestOverlayRect (state-agnostic) + windowing math; extract a generic renderOverlayWindow(rows,selected,windowRows,...) instead of copying renderSuggestPanel.
- sentHistory []string on tuiModel appended in startAIWithDisplay when sent!="" && sent==display (excludes skill bodies and slash commands), last-entry dedupe, cap MaxHistorySize=500; DO NOT merge Session.Messages (pruned, commits only at turn end, and stores skill display strings like "⚙ /cmd" via replaceNewestUserText).
- Register keys under a new scopeHistory in keymap.go (scopeComposer does not bind up/down; enter/esc/tab exist in other scopes so folding in would duplicate); use a curated probe in keymap_probe_test.go, do not add historyState to the default fingerprint sweep (breaks TestEveryBoundKeyIsRegistered).

## What did not work
- Empty-history guard is mandatory: navigation with wrap math does %len -> div-by-zero panic on a fresh session; opening Up must not be consumed (return false,false,nil) or TestScrollAccept_EmptyDashboardDoesNotSwallowArrowKeys fails.
- Overlay rows MUST be sanitized: renderDialogFrame/sliceANSI preserves CSI/OSC escape sequences (x/ansi v0.11.6), so pasted text can clear the screen or write the system clipboard; pass entries through SafeChatBlockText(entry,0) + newline->'⏎' normalization.
- sentHistory must reset on every session-identity change (/clear, beginNewSession, openSessionInfo, runLoadSlash, startup resume) or the previous session's text leaks into the next session's picker.
- Navigation should stop at boundaries (matching InputBuffer/bash), not wrap like the suggest popup; Down at the newest dismisses back to the untouched draft.

## Why
The investigation + hostile validation (ADLC Step 0) produced concrete, reusable facts and traps for any future internal/cli TUI work: key-routing seams (handleChatKey order), overlay rendering pipeline (renderDialogFrame/overlayAt/suggestOverlayRect), session message lifecycle (pruning, replaceNewestUserText, MessagesCopy lock contract), and the keymap registry/probe enforcement (INV-TUI-23/27).

scope: project

## Summary
memory_search is NOT a token index: it runs LIKE '%<whole query>%' over lower(title|summary|content). Multi-word queries whose words aren't verbatim-contiguous in stored text return 0 hits (e.g. "DeepSeek v4-flash HTTP 400" → 0 though the phrase exists separated by ": transient "). Single tokens work; token-AND finds entries. modernc.org/sqlite v1.54.0 has ENABLE_FTS5 but no trigram/ICU.

## What worked
- Empirical probe against a copy of the real db reproduced all 0-hit queries and showed single tokens and token-AND match
- PRAGMA compile_options on modernc.org/sqlite v1.54.0: ENABLE_FTS5 present, no TRIGRAM, no ICU
- Baseline: go test ./internal/memory/... green; existing tests only use single-token queries, so token-AND is backwards compatible

## What did not work
- Multi-word natural queries silently return [] — no error, no hint, no relaxation
- No stemming, no token frequency, no phrase proximity; SQL lower() is ASCII-only
- Tool docs ("by keywords") contradict implementation (exact contiguous phrase)

## Why
User reported the memory search index as unreliable; probe against a copy of the real .mivia/memory.db proved the root cause is query semantics, not data: whole-phrase contiguous-substring matching. Ranking is a 4-level CASE (title exact > title contains > summary > content), then created DESC/title ASC; tool description says "by keywords" while behavior demands exact contiguous phrases, so agents naturally send multi-word queries that fail. Fix: tokenize query, require all tokens (AND) as per-token substrings, keep phrase bonuses, fall back to whole-phrase LIKE when no tokens remain; keep backend parity (search_parity_test.go pins sqlite vs in-memory equivalence).

scope: project
verdict: good
tags: windows, packages.Load, GOCACHE, environment-filtering, codeintel, wine
created: 2026-08-10

## Summary
On Windows, cmd/go locates its build cache via GOCACHE or %LocalAppData%\go-build. A filtered env for go subprocesses that drops LOCALAPPDATA (and lacks GOCACHE, which go test never exports) makes every `go list`/packages.Load die with "build cache is required, but could not be located", yielding zero packages — misreported as "symbol not found". Unix masks it via $HOME/.cache/go-build.

## What worked
- Reproduced the CI failure under wine with a real GOOS=windows test binary; the Linux ELF "probe" binary had silently run natively, not under wine (checked with `file`).\n- Driver-level probe (exec go list with the filtered env) surfaced the exact error text instead of guessing.\n- EqualFold matching for Windows env keys avoids the case trap (LOCALAPPDATA vs LocalAppData).

## What did not work
- First attempt added "LocalAppData" (title case) to the allowlist — did nothing because the real var is LOCALAPPDATA.\n- Debugging through the analyzer's "symbol not found" error wasted time; the load errors are swallowed by design.

## Why
internal/codeintel/analyzerEnv() filtered os.Environ() to a small allowlist to block network access. The allowlist had "LocalAppData" (title case) while Windows sets LOCALAPPDATA, so the variable was dropped; all codeintel symbol queries then failed on Windows CI while passing on Linux/macOS. Fix: pass LOCALAPPDATA through with case-insensitive (EqualFold) matching. Also: `go test` does NOT export GOCACHE/GOMODCACHE/GOROOT to test binaries (verified empirically), and `go test -c` without GOOS=windows builds a HOST (Linux) binary even with a .exe name — verify with `file` before running under wine.

# mivia tool-result context pipeline: spool/ref machinery and gaps

scope: project
verdict: neutral
tags: context-management, tool-results, contentrefs, compaction, elision, architecture
created: 2026-08-12

## Summary
mivia already degrades oversized tool results to content refs (remainder.Spool + contentref + read_output, principal-scoped grants, ledger-backed in prod). Gaps vs industry practice: elision in contextmgr drops bodies irreversibly (no ref), batch budget and per-call caps default OFF, inline-vs-ref decision spread across 4+ sites with independent thresholds, no summary layer.

## What worked
- contentref is a single canonical minter (ref:kind:digest)
- remainder.Spool enforces principal-scoped grants + INV-AG-10 (ref only after store)
- shapeBatch degrades batch results to refs, never fails; derive from prompt budget works
- read_output pages 32 KiB with status not_found/denied/expired
- dual head+tail capture exists for run_command

## What did not work
- contextmgr elideToolResults replaces old bodies with a notice that names no ref (bytes lost, compaction irreversible)
- shipped defaults: MaxToolResultChars=0, BatchResultBudgetBytes=0 -> long sessions grow context to compaction trigger
- thresholds duplicated: elision floor 2048, BatchDegradeFloorBytes 16KiB, inline_output_bytes 4096, read_output page 32KiB
- no summary layer for large tool results (head-only inline is a poor summary for search/grep)
- always-ref would cost an extra LLM turn per fetch and relies on model fetch discipline

## Why
The "replace all tool outputs with refs" idea is half-implemented. Ground truth: pass1 per-call cap (CapWithSpoolRef, MaxToolResultChars default 0=uncapped), pass2 batch budget (BatchResultBudgetBytes default 0=off, -1 derives quarter of prompt budget), compaction at 80% of max_prompt_tokens with elision of old >2KiB bodies into a non-retrievable notice, retention at 50% target. Subagent outputs use inline_output_bytes (default 4096) then output_ref. Refs add a full LLM turn per fetch (latency), and models that do not fetch cause thrashing; industry (Anthropic) uses summary+stored-full and reversible compaction, not always-ref.

The controller has no agent registry, so it can never resolve a routing digest — synthesizing there is architecturally impossible to do correctly. Added --force to mivia workflow delete (and the agenttools delete tool) so runs stranded by a dead executor (pending/running/waiting_approval) can be purged; live claims are still refused. Fixed controller resume so agent_panel steps without a StepRuntime are no longer a hard error.

- Force flag plumbed through every Delete surface (agenttools tool + service + types, localengine, session engine, CLI command, TUI dialog) so behavior is consistent everywhere.

- The linear_execution.go resume path previously treated missing StepRuntime for agent_panel as a hard error; only agent/agent_gate truly need a snapshotted runtime (panel members run through the PanelCoordinator and are re-joined via advancePanelStep).

A zombie wfr-... run could previously block deletion forever: non-terminal statuses were refused and there was no force override, and a controller regression made resume of agent_panel steps (which legitimately carry no StepRuntime — members re-join via advancePanelStep's findResumablePanelAttempt D14 path) fail with a hard error, leaving a run wedged in-flight. The force path mirrors resume/deliver --force: it unlocks only the status gate; claim fencing (live claim refused, expired lease taken over) is untouched so an actively executing run can never be deleted. # bug-fix workflow built: engine facts, limits 0/0, review-driven fixes

scope: project
verdict: good
tags: workflow, bug-fix, bug-audit, feature-delivery, engine-capabilities
created: 2026-08-11

## Summary
Delivered .mivia/workflows/bug-fix.toml + 8 templates + 4 schemas: a dedicated bug-hunt-and-fix workflow (auditor hunt -> reviewer triage -> engineer fix -> review -> optional perf gate -> host gates -> draft PR), validated by the compiler, reviewed pre- and post-implementation by dispatched agents, with limits now unlimited (0/0) and 1 MiB inputs per request.

## What worked
- Built .mivia/workflows/bug-fix.toml: hunt(auditor/bug-audit) -> triage(reviewer/bug-audit, verdicts confirmed|insufficient_evidence|no_bug) -> fix_plan -> implement -> review(secure-change, echoes has_perf) -> conditional perf_verify(performance/performance-review) -> go gates -> draft PR delivery.
- Verified engine facts: transition matchers compare STRING output values of the FROM step only, so branch fields must be string enums (has_perf "true"/"false"); inputs are string-only (max 1 MiB, definition.MaxInputBytes); max_step_attempts=0 and max_duration_seconds=0 are legal and mean unlimited (no unbounded-cycle guard fires because every loop has max_iterations>0); jschema enforces maxItems (findings capped at 2 machine-enforced); failed evidence gates emit AttemptStatusFailed (evidence_host_failure_test.go:36), so match={status="failed"} is correct; delivery re-entry steps MUST bind delivery.failure (compiler-enforced); no-diff delivery gate settles runs with no PR when nothing changed (no_bug path is safe).
- Post-implementation review (reviewer + verifier) caught 3 real issues, all fixed: plan-v1.json requires addressed_findings (fix-plan template now instructs []), title_template must be policy-safe (changed to static 'fix: bug-fix delivery'), repair template now lists PR scopes.
- Pre-existing main-tree WIP in internal/provider|reasoning (from an earlier .claude session) makes check_go_structure --strict fail in the MAIN tree, but workflow runs are isolated in .mivia/worktrees/workflow-wfr-* so their gates are unaffected.

## What did not work
- A reviewer agent's 'critical' finding about evidence-gate failure semantics (status=failed vs succeeded+output.status=failed) was wrong; the engine's own tests refute it. Lesson: verify engine semantics from controller tests before changing workflow shape.
- No-bug runs settle via the no-diff delivery gate (run succeeds, no PR) - there is NO custom terminal; a 'no_bug' terminal is not implementable in a workflow file.
- 1 MiB input bindings can overflow the reviewer agent's 262K-token window if an operator passes a near-1 MiB task; caps are ceilings, but this is a documented tradeoff.

## Why
Record the engine constraints discovered (string-only matchers, 0/0 limits semantics, delivery.failure binding, no-diff gate) and the review-driven fixes so future workflow authoring in this repo skips the verification loop.
